newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Q4 bond programme keeps market guessing.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Q4 bond programme keeps market guessing.

text.p: The Dutch Ministry of Finance is expected to issue a new 10-year bond or reopen an existing issue to finish its 1996 borrowing programme but may keep the market guessing about it until the national budget on September 17.
Economists and traders said the ministry was more likely to opt for a new 10-year line if the balance of the funding task was around the 12.7 billion guilders estimated by some.
But they said if the gap was narrower, as some suspected it would be, the ministry might consider reopening one of its tap issues including the new September 2002 bond launched last week.
The ministry declined to comment.
"We never comment on which way we will collect money," a spokesman for the ministry told Reuters.
The borrowing requirement set out by the ministry earlier this year was 40.8 million guilders, consisting of the budget deficit of 21.1 billion and redemptions of 19.7 billion.
A total of 28.1 billion guilders has been raised, including 7.5 billion with the September 2002 tap issue last week.

Analysts said stronger than expected economic growth may have trimmed the budget deficit from its forecast level and redemptions could be partly funded from the state's cash reserves held at the central bank.
Government sources have confirmed the ministry will use the cash surplus, which has peaked as high as 15 billion guilders in the last year, to cut government debt through to 1997.
They said an announcement on whether the funds would be used for redemptions or to replace borrowing planned for the fourth quarter may be made with the budget next month.
ING economist Henk de Bruijne said the ministry might choose to reopen the 2002 issue and boost outstandings to 15 billion guilders, the level needed to make it a five-year benchmark.
He said the 1996 budget deficit could be 2.0-3.0 billion guilders lower than forecast due to the strong economy.
"In that case, we do not see another new issue," he said.
BZW bond strategist Phyllis Reed said the Netherlands was less vulnerable than other European countries to overshoot budget deficit targets.
A capital markets trader said if the funding gap was as low as 8.0 billion guilders due to a lower budget shortfall, this sum could be funded by reopening the September 2002 issue.
"With an extra 7.0-8.0 billion, you have a good benchmark," he said.
But Mark van der Kroft of ABN AMRO said he expected a new 10-year bond to be issued in the final quarter of 1996.
He cited the response to the September 2002 bond, which struggled to attract buyers until the Bundesbank announced a surprise repo cut on the final day of the sale last Friday.
Most of the funds were raised on the last day though the sale price was raised eight times. And it still finished below the initial tap price.
"They must have learnt the market was looking for a new 10-year benchmark," van der Kroft said.
Leo Kranenburg of Generale Bank agreed, saying such an issue would easily raise 10.0-12.0 billion guilders.
-- Garry West, Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000
